goals.0: Names of everyday food and drinks
goals.1: The forms of essen and trinken (du isst!)
goals.3: Talking about your own eating habits
dialog.0.de.1.n: du isst — essen is irregular (e → i)
dialog.0.de.3.n: gern = gladly, with pleasure — it comes after the verb
dialog.1.de.2.n: Ich esse gern … = I like eating …
dialog.3.de.0.n: Coffee, tea, water — all take trinken (to drink), not essen
grammar.0.intro: essen is irregular: with du and er, e → i. trinken is regular.
grammar.0.note: du isst — not „du esst“! The s and the st merge into isst.
grammar.1.title: gern — “like to / gladly”
grammar.1.text: gern after the verb shows that you like doing something: „Ich esse gern Reis.“ (I like eating rice), „Ich trinke gern Tee.“ In German you don't need a separate verb (“to love”) — gern is enough.
grammar.2.title: essen or trinken?
grammar.2.text: Solid food = essen (Brot, Reis, Fisch, Fleisch, Gemüse, Apfel). Liquids = trinken (Wasser, Tee, Kaffee, Milch). In Bangla we say “eat tea” (“cha khawa”), but in German it is always „Tee trinken“ (to drink).
quiz.6.why: gern comes after the verb: Ich esse gern Reis.
quiz.7.prompt: Put the words in order: “I like drinking tea.”
